svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Five balls launched at the same speed (20 m/s) at 15\u00b0, 30\u00b0, 45\u00b0, 60\u00b0 and 75\u00b0, with no air resistance."], [1, "Each follows a parabola: horizontal velocity stays constant while gravity accelerates the ball downwards."], [4.5, "45\u00b0 gives the greatest range. 30\u00b0 and 60\u00b0 land at the same place, and so do 15\u00b0 and 75\u00b0."], [7, "The steeper launches go higher and stay up longer, but travel more slowly sideways."]]
svg.title: Projectile motion at different angles
svg.desc: Trajectories for the same launch speed at 15°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 75°. The 45° launch has the greatest range; complementary angles have equal ranges.
svg.text: Projectile motion: launch angle and range
v = 20 m/s, g = 9.8 m/s², no air resistance. Scale: 1 m = 22 px.

g.data-info: With no air resistance each path is a parabola: constant horizontal velocity, constant downward acceleration g.
Range R = v² sin 2θ / g is greatest when sin 2θ = 1, i.e. θ = 45°: 40.8 m for 20 m/s.
30° and 60° (and 15° and 75°) give the same range, because sin 2θ is the same; the steeper one goes higher and stays in the air longer.
H = v² sin² θ / 2g: greatest for the steepest launch.
